note: Hand-assembled and change-checked officer by officer. 19 offices across two counties that do NOT elect the same set, because each is governed by its own special law.

statutes.general_rule: Minn. Stat. § 382.01 — every county elects an auditor, treasurer, sheriff, recorder, attorney and coroner, four-year terms beginning the first Monday in January next succeeding the election. NEITHER of these counties matches it.
statutes.ramsey: Minn. Stat. § 383A.20 subd. 2(a) — the auditor, treasurer, court commissioner and recorder are appointive, not elective. Ramsey is Minnesota's only home rule charter county.
statutes.st_louis: Minn. Stat. § 383C.136 — the treasurer's office was abolished in 1969 and its functions transferred to the auditor; the recorder became appointive in 1991.
statutes.commissioners: Minn. Stat. § 375.01 — commissioners serve four years 'and until their successors qualify'. ⚠ This gives NO statutory day, which is why commissioner starts here are less precise than the constitutional officers'.
statutes.coroner: Neither county elects one. Ramsey's medical examiner is appointed by the board; St. Louis contracts with the Midwest Medical Examiner's Office.

change_check.method: sweep-county-pages.mjs — both the MN-2 word signal and the MN-3 expired-date signal, over every page, each controlled.

roster.page_note: His page states he was 'sworn in as Sheriff on January 10, 2023'. That is the CEREMONY. Minn. Stat. § 382.01 begins the term on the first Monday in January next succeeding the election, which is 2023-01-02, and that is what is recorded.

roster.title: County Attorney
roster.page_note: Won unopposed in 2022 with 98.95%. Her page writes 'Kim Maki'; the ballot name is Kimberly J. Maki.

roster.title: Auditor/Treasurer
roster.page_note: 🔴 Her page says she was 'sworn in on January 3, 2019' — that is her FIRST term, not the current one. She was re-elected 2022-11-08, 60,787 to 13,838. This is the Nelsie Yang trap from MN-3: a page stating the first swearing-in reads as a term start and is not one. The title is Auditor/Treasurer because § 383C.136 abolished the treasurer in 1969 and gave its functions to the auditor.

roster.title: Commissioner, District 1
roster.page_note: Her page says she 'began her term in January 2025' and gives no day.

roster.title: Commissioner, District 2
roster.page_note: Her page says only 'has served on the Ramsey County Board since 2012', which is her FIRST year and not the current term. She won the general on 2024-11-05.

roster.title: Commissioner, District 3
roster.predecessor_note: 🔴 A SPECIAL ELECTION, and the only mid-term change in either county. Trista Martinson resigned; McMurtrey won the special on 2025-02-11 and 'began his term in February 2025'. He is the first Black man elected to a county board in Minnesota. A blanket 'elected 2024' would have been wrong for this seat.

roster.title: Commissioner, District 4
roster.precision_note: ⚠ PRECISION CORRECTED 2026-09-15, before CC_0112 was written. This row previously read 2023-01-02 at 'day'. That is Minn. Stat. § 382.01's first Monday in January, which governs the CONSTITUTIONAL OFFICERS and NOT the board: § 375.01 gives a commissioner four years 'and until their successors qualify', and qualification happens at the board's organizational meeting, which is why St. Louis's own published expiries land on a Monday in one cohort and a Tuesday in the other. No page states a day for this seat. The month is certain — the term begins in January following the November election — so the row is written at 'month'. Writing the day would have asserted the exact date this wave disproved.

roster.title: Commissioner, District 6
roster.page_note: 🔴 Her page says she was 'elected in 2023', and Minnesota county commissioners are elected in EVEN years — which read as a special election and is not one. She assumed office on 2023-01-02, having been elected in November 2022. A biography's loose phrasing is not an election record.
